paper_metadata.title: Oxidation behaviour of candidate alloys in high-temperature helium-rich environments

evidence.quote: Several superalloys with high corrosion resistance and superior mechanical strength are potential structural materials for HTGR intermediate heat exchanger component.
three nickel-based alloys (Alloy 617, Alloy 625, and Hastelloy X) and one iron-based alloy (Alloy 800H) were selected and underwent corrosion tests.

evidence.quote: However, in the two humid helium environments, needle-shaped oxide particles were present and particularly abundant in the 50% humidity environment, as shown in Figure 9 . The oxide layer was mainly composed of MnCr 2O4, TiO2, and Cr 2O3.

evidence.section: Results and discussion - Surface and cross-sectional oxide morphologies

evidence.section: Results and discussion - Surface and cross-sectional oxide morphologies
evidence.quote: According to Figures 10 and 11, internal oxidation of Al led to the formation of Al 2O3 underneath the oxide layer, but the amount of Al 2O3 in Alloy 625 was much less than those in Alloy 800H and Alloy 617 due to the lower Al content in this alloy.

evidence.section: Results and discussion - Surface and cross-sectional oxide morphologies
evidence.quote: In addition to uniform distribution of oxide particles, ridges of oxide formed along the grain boundaries of this alloy in all four controlled helium environments. In particular, Ti existed on the grain boundary ridges in the form of TiO 2 in pure helium and 90% helium with 10% oxygen environments

evidence.section: Results and discussion - Surface and cross-sectional oxide morphologies
evidence.quote: In humid helium environments, nodules of Si-rich oxide particles formed additionally on the surface, and the size and the number of the nodules increased with increasing test duration.

evidence.section: Results and discussion - Surface and cross-sectional oxide morphologies
evidence.quote: The surface oxides of Alloy 617 were mainly MnCr 2O4, TiO2 and Cr 2O3, and ridges of oxide also formed along the grain boundaries of this alloy.

evidence.section: Results and discussion - Surface and cross-sectional oxide morphologies
evidence.quote: In the two helium environments containing water vapour, the surface oxide layer was also covered with Si-rich oxide particles (shown in Figure 7 ), and the size and the number increased with increasing test duration.

evidence.section: Results and discussion - Mass gain analyses
evidence.quote: The mass gain of Alloy 800H was the highest, and that of Hastelloy X was the lowest among the four alloys under all test conditions.

evidence.section: Results and discussion - Mass gain analyses
evidence.quote: The mass gain of Alloy 800H was the highest, and that of Hastelloy X was the lowest among the four alloys under all test conditions.

Internal oxidation is the process in which oxygen diffuses inward into the substrate and reacts with a certain active element in an alloy. Except for Hastelloy X, internal oxides of Al2O3 could be found near the Cr 2O3-alloy interface of the other alloys.
Internal oxidation was observed underneath the grain boundaries of Alloy 800H, Alloy 617, and Alloy 625 and possibly resulted in oxide ridges on the surfaces of these alloys.
